Rainilaiarivony: Prime Minister of Madagascar from 1864 to 1895.
Before circling the Moon 45 times as command module pilot on Apollo 12, this naval aviator had already flown in space piloting Gemini 11 — which astronaut?
Richard F. Gordon Jr.: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1929–2017)
Appointed Deputy to the Führer, this Nazi leader stunned everyone by flying solo to Scotland in 1941 to try to negotiate Britain out of the war — who was he?

This Indian Army major with the National Security Guard's elite commando unit was killed in action during the 2008 Mumbai attacks and posthumously received India's highest peacetime gallantry award — who was he?

Once a member of the State Duma, this Russian financial fraudster's donation-based scheme defrauded thousands of investors — and he later claimed the same scheme was behind a bitcoin price rally — who is he?
Ending on the Fourth of July, 1863, this brutal Mississippi River campaign saw Grant trap Pemberton's Confederates in a fortress city — completing the Anaconda Plan's grip on the river. What was it?
Siege of Vicksburg: Battle of the American Civil War.
Son of a Greek Catholic priest in Galicia, he led a radical faction of Ukrainian nationalists and orchestrated the 1934 assassination of a Polish interior minister — who was he?
A former brigadier-general who rose to Speaker of Singapore's Parliament, this politician resigned in 2023 after admitting to a years-long affair with a fellow MP — who is he?
Tan Chuan-Jin: Singaporean politician. Tan Chuan-Jin (born 10 January 1969) is a Singaporean former politician and brigadier-general.
Brother of King Henry VIII's third wife, this nobleman married the king's widow Catherine Parr in 1547 while sparring with his own brother for influence over the young King Edward VI — who was he?
Thomas Seymour, 1st Baron Seymour of Sudeley
Thomas Seymour, 1st Baron Seymour of Sudeley: English nobleman (1508–1548)
Thomas Seymour, 1st Baron Seymour of Sudeley
This Indian politician served as Maharashtra's 19th chief minister from 2019 to 2022 while also editing a newspaper for over a decade — who is he?
Uddhav Thackeray: 19th Chief Minister of Maharashtra from 2019 to 2022 (born 1960)
In 1976, this Soviet pilot defected to the West by flying his MiG-25 'Foxbat' jet interceptor to Japan, handing the CIA what George H. W. Bush called an 'intelligence bonanza' — who is he?
Viktor Belenko: Soviet pilot who defected to the West (1947–2023)

Beginning with the 1916 death of Yuan Shikai, this chaotic decade-plus in Chinese history saw the country splinter under rival military cliques until Sun Yat-sen's Nationalists challenged the Beijing government for legitimacy — which period?
Warlord Era: Period in the history of the Republic of China (1916–1928)

Convinced that Protestants and the Catholic majority had to make common cause against the Crown, this revolutionary helped found the Society of United Irishmen in 1791 and became an icon of Irish republicanism — who was he?
A career Army general who became a national hero in the Mexican-American War, this 12th U.S. president died of a stomach illness just 16 months into office — who is he?
Zachary Taylor: President of the United States from 1849 to 1850.
Which of these people was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Qian Xuesen (born 1911) is the earliest of the four. Qian received his undergraduate education in mechanical engineering at National Chiao Tung University in Shanghai in 1934.
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as an astronomer?
Arthur Eddington is an astronomer. Sir Arthur Stanley Eddington (28 December 1882 – 22 November 1944) was an English astrophysicist and mathematician.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Shakuntala Devi is a mathematician. Shakuntala Devi (4 November 1929 – 21 April 2013) was an Indian mental calculator, astrologer, and writer, popularly known as the "Human Computer".
What is the atomic number of Xenon?
Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
What is the atomic number of Unbibium?
Unbibium, also known as element 122 or eka-thorium, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has placeholder symbol Ubb and atomic number 122.
In what year was Mario Molina born?
Mario Molina: Mario José Molina-Pasquel Henríquez (19 March 1943 – 7 October 2020) was a Mexican physical chemist.
In what year was Nikolai Patrushev born?
Nikolai Patrushev: Patrushev has spoken favorably of the rise of KGB stalwarts to the highest echelons of power of Russia, referring to them as the "new nobility".
In what year was Johannes Gutenberg born?
Johannes Gutenberg: Johannes Gensfleisch zur Laden zum Gutenberg (c. 1393–1406 – 3 February 1468) was a German inventor and craftsman who invented the movable-type printing press.
In what year did Ferruccio Lamborghini die?
Ferruccio Lamborghini: In 1959, he opened an oil burner factory, Lamborghini Bruciatori, which later entered the business of producing air conditioning equipment.
In what year did Archimedes die?
Archimedes died during the siege of Syracuse, when he was killed by a Roman soldier despite orders that he should not be harmed.
In what year was Hydrogen discovered?
Hydrogen is a chemical element; it has the symbol H and atomic number 1.
Mil Mi-8: Mil Moscow Helicopter Plant. The Mi-8 is the world's most-produced helicopter, with over 17,000 units used by over 50 countries.
Semen: prostate. Semen, also known as seminal fluid, is a bodily fluid that contains spermatozoa from the male gonads of animals.
In which country is Thalidomide scandal?
Thalidomide scandal: Germany. It was introduced as a sedative and medication for morning sickness without having been tested on pregnant women.
Who is credited with discovering Flerovium?
Flerovium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.
Who is credited with discovering Hypochlorous acid?
Hypochlorous acid: Antoine Jérôme Balard. Hypochlorous acid is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula ClOH, also written as HClO, HOCl, or ClHO.
Who is credited with discovering Gallium?
Gallium: Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran. Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.
Sometimes called ajowan caraway or carom, this annual herb in the carrot family produces a seed-like fruit often confused with lovage — what is it?
Ajwain (Trachyspermum ammi) - also known as ajowan caraway, thymol seeds, bishop's weed, or carom - is an annual herb in the family Apiaceae.

With more than 140 species spread across 16 genera in oceans worldwide, these small forage fish are usually classified as oily fish, and a few South American species live only in fresh water — name this fish?
Anchovy are small, common forage fish of the family Engraulidae.
Native to Europe and Asia, which genus of burdock plants owes its seed-dispersal success to burrs that later inspired a famous fastening invention?
Arctium is a genus of biennial plants commonly known as burdock, family Asteraceae.
This American physicist shared the 2017 Nobel with Rainer Weiss and Kip Thorne for decisive contributions to LIGO and the observation of gravitational waves — who is he?
Barry Barish (born January 27, 1936) is an American experimental physicist and Nobel Laureate.

Thought to be the world's most abundant bird of prey in its family, with an estimated 6.7 million individuals, this opportunistic raptor is known for its angled wings and distinctive forked tail — what is it?
Black kite (Milvus migrans) is a medium-sized bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors.
Meaning 'thunder lizard' in Greek, this sauropod dinosaur genus was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1879 from a partial, skull-less skeleton found in Wyoming's Como Bluff — what dinosaur is it?

Brontosaurus (literally 'thunder lizard', from the Greek words bront, 'thunder', and saros, 'lizard') is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived in present-day United States during the Late Jurassic period.
From starch that stores energy to the cellulose that stiffens plants and the chitin in insect shells, this biomolecule family is essentially sugars and their derivatives — what is it?
Carbohydrate is a sugar (saccharide) or a sugar derivative.

The smallest recognized dog breed in the world, this Mexican toy breed has large erect ears and a rounded skull, and its genes carry a trace of pre-Columbian indigenous American dog ancestry — which breed?

Chihuahua (dog breed) is a Mexican breed of toy dog and the smallest recognized dog breed in the world. It is primarily kept as a companion animal and is characterized by its compact size, large erect ears, and rounded skull.
Native to Africa, Arabia and India, this semi-succulent herb smells like oregano and is known by names like Spanish thyme and Mexican mint — which plant?
Coleus amboinicus is a species of semi-succulent perennial plant in the family Lamiaceae.

This interdisciplinary field, whose name combines a Latin word for 'accusation' with a Greek suffix meaning 'study of,' draws on sociology, psychology, economics, and law to examine crime and deviant behavior. What field is this?
Criminology (from Latin crimen, 'accusation', and Ancient Greek -, -logia, from logos, 'word, reason') is the interdisciplinary study of crime and deviant behaviour.
This colourless, highly volatile, sweet-smelling organic compound with formula (CH3CH2)2O was once used as a general anesthetic and remains a common laboratory solvent — what is it?

This American theoretical physicist, a professor emeritus at Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study, is renowned for foundational contributions to string theory and topological quantum field theory — who is he?
Edward Witten (born August 26, 1951) is an American theoretical physicist known for his contributions to string theory, topological quantum field theory, and various areas of mathematics.
The major female sex hormone, this estrogen steroid drives the development of breasts and a female pattern of fat distribution and regulates the menstrual cycle — which one is it?
Estradiol (E2), also called oestrogen, oestradiol, is an estrogen steroid hormone and the major female sex hormone.

Sometimes mistakenly called a cat despite belonging to the weasel family, this North American forest-dwelling carnivore is the only living species in its genus and is larger than the martens it resembles — what animal is it?
Fisher (animal) (Pekania pennanti) is a carnivorous mammal native to North America, a forest-dwelling creature whose range covers much of the boreal forest in Canada to the northern United States.
Practitioners of this discipline monitor crustal motion, tides, and polar shifts to maintain accurate global positioning reference frames — what is this field called?
Geodesy (jee-) or geodetics is the science of measuring and representing the geometry, gravity, and spatial orientation of the Earth in temporally varying 3D space.
One of only two wild camelid species native to South America, this llama relative lives at lower elevations than its cousin, the vicuña — what is it called?
Guanaco (gwah-; Lama guanicoe) is a camelid native to South America, closely related to the domesticated llama.
Never approved by any drug regulator, this THC-like compound made by hydrogenating cannabis isomers has been sold in head-shop vaporizers since the early 2020s — what is it?
Hexahydrocannabinol (HHC) is a phytocannabinoid that has been reported as a minor component of Cannabis oleoresin.
About the size of an almond in humans, this small brain region links the nervous system to the endocrine system via the pituitary gland — what is it?
Hypothalamus (pl.: hypothalami; from Ancient Greek (hup) 'under' and (thlamos) 'chamber') is a small part of the vertebrate brain that contains a number of nuclei with a variety of functions.
Serving as president of the European Commission from 1985 to 1995, this French politician played a central role in creating the European single market and laying groundwork for the euro — who is he?
Jacques Delors (20 July 1925 - 27 December 2023) was a French politician who served as president of the European Commission from 1985 to 1995.
Named after a 19th-century English physicist, this SI unit of energy equals the work done when a one-newton force moves an object one metre in the direction of that force — name the unit?
Joule (JOOL, or JOWL; symbol: J) is the unit of energy in the International System of Units (SI).
What reddish-brown, alcohol-based tincture of opium, roughly 10% opium by weight, was historically sold without a prescription as a pain reliever and cough suppressant until the early 20th century?
Laudanum is a tincture of opium containing approximately 10% powdered opium by weight (the equivalent of 1% morphine).
Used since pre-Columbian times as a pack animal that can haul about a quarter of its body weight for miles, which domesticated South American camelid has wool low in lanolin?
Llama (Spanish) (Lama glama) is a domesticated South American camelid, widely used as a meat and pack animal by Andean cultures since the pre-Columbian era.
Though it's the strongest bone in the face, this lower jawbone tends to deform with age and is prone to fractures — what is it called?

Mandible (from the Latin mandibula, 'for chewing'), lower jaw, or jawbone is a bone that makes up the lower - and typically more mobile - component of the mouth (the upper jaw being known as the maxilla).

Patented in 1922 and used to relieve pain, fever, and spasms, this drug's sale is restricted in some countries due to a rare but serious blood-cell side effect discovered in the 1970s — what drug is it?
Metamizole is a painkiller, spasm reliever, and fever reliever drug.
Found naturally in the dark resin of opium and given everywhere from pills to spinal injections, this opiate alters how the brain feels pain — what is it?
Morphine is an opiate found naturally in opium, a dark brown resin produced by drying the latex of opium poppies (Papaver somniferum).
This multidisciplinary field studies the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves — their function and their disorders — blending physiology, anatomy, and more — name the field?
Neuroscience is the scientific study of the nervous system (the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nervous system), its functions, and its disorders.
In this learning process, voluntary behaviors grow more frequent through reinforcement or fade through punishment and extinction — what is it called?
Operant conditioning is a learning process in which voluntary behaviors are modified by association with the addition (or removal) of reward or aversive stimuli.
Combining medicine with comedy, this physician organizes volunteers to clown around for orphans and patients worldwide through a nonprofit institute he founded in 1989 — who is he?
Patch Adams (born May 28, 1945) is an American physician, comedian, social activist, clown, and author.
Ranging in color from clear to yellow, green, or even grey, this respiratory mucus is expelled through coughing and also goes by the name sputum — what is it?
Phlegm (Ancient) is mucus produced by the respiratory system, excluding that produced by the throat and nose passages.
Abundant throughout the plant kingdom, this broad class of naturally occurring phenolic compounds includes flavonoids and ellagitannin — what is the family called?
Polyphenol are a large family of naturally occurring phenols.

This psychiatric state describes an inability to distinguish reality from delusion, marked by symptoms like hallucinations and disorganized thinking, and can stem from conditions like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder — name the state?
Psychosis is the inability to distinguish what is or is not real.

This genus of roughly 60 herbaceous perennials in the buckwheat family includes the familiar pie vegetable prized for its tart stalks despite mildly toxic leaves — which genus, native to Europe and Asia?
Rheum (plant) is a genus of about 60 herbaceous perennial plants in the family Polygonaceae.
This grayish-leaved, purple-flowered evergreen subshrub is a Mediterranean member of the mint family, long used both as a culinary herb and an ornamental garden plant — what plant is it?
Salvia officinalis is a perennial, evergreen subshrub, with woody stems, grayish leaves, and blue to purplish flowers.

This dog breed from southern China, traditionally kept as a property guardian, was driven to the brink of extinction in the 20th century and is known in the West for its deep wrinkles. What breed is this?

Shar Pei (Cantonese; pinyin: sh p) is a dog breed from
southern China.
This family of roughly 1,450 moth species, with narrow wings and streamlined bodies built for fast, hovering flight, are so nimble they're routinely mistaken for hummingbirds — what are they called?
Sphingidae are a family of moths commonly called sphinx moths, also colloquially known as hawk moths, with many of their caterpillars known as hornworms.
These large waterfowl of the genus Cygnus are close relatives of geese and ducks, and are known for typically mating for life. What birds are they?
Swan are birds of the genus Cygnus within the family Anatidae.
Classed among the saurischians and placing them nearer to sauropodomorphs than to ornithischians, these hollow-boned, three-toed dinosaurs were ancestrally meat-eaters — which clade?
Theropoda (from ancient Greek -) is one of the three major clades of dinosaur, alongside Ornithischia and Sauropodomorpha.

Native only to New Zealand and resembling a lizard, this reptile is the sole surviving member of an order that was hugely diverse in the Mesozoic era, with fossils dating to the Middle Triassic — what's the animal?
Tuatara (Mori:; Sphenodon punctatus) is a species of reptile endemic to New Zealand.

First described by John Edward Gray in 1821, this family of small feliform mammals spans Africa, southern Europe, and Asia on both sides of the Wallace Line, and includes the genets — name the family?
Viverridae is a family of small to medium-sized feliform mammals, comprising 14 genera with 33 species.
Native from Panama to southern Canada, this plant genus of 50 species belongs to the asparagus family alongside the agaves — name the genus?
Yucca (YUK-) is both the scientific name and common name for a genus native to North America from Panama to southern Canada.
This protrusion in the neck, formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage around the larynx, becomes more prominent in most men during puberty — what is it?
Adam's apple: Feature of the neck. The Adam's apple is the protrusion in the neck formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage surrounding the larynx, typically visible in men and less so in women.

This organic functional group, structured R−CH=O and alternatively called a formyl group when isolated from its side chain, appears throughout biologically and technologically important chemicals — what is it?
Aldehyde: Organic compound containing the functional group R–CH=O.

Once sold as Elavil, this tricyclic antidepressant is now often a second-line choice — used as much for neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia, and migraines as for depression, thanks to its many side effects. Which drug?
Amitriptyline: Tricyclic antidepressant. Due to the frequency and prominence of side effects, amitriptyline is generally considered a second-line therapy for these indications.
This British-American theoretical physicist at the University of Illinois won the 2003 Nobel Prize for pioneering work on superfluidity and the quantum physics of low-temperature helium — who was he?
Painting, sculpture, and architecture are its three classical visual branches, yet nobody can agree on a single definition for it; what cultural pursuit of creative and imaginative talent is this?
Art: Creative work to evoke aesthetic response.
The world's largest nocturnal primate, this Madagascar lemur has ever-growing rodent-like teeth and taps tree trunks with a bony middle finger to fish out grubs by echo — which animal?
Aye-aye: Species of primate. This foraging method is called percussive foraging, and takes up 5–41% of the aye-aye's foraging time.
Named after the aromatic resin from which it was first derived, this simplest aromatic carboxylic compound forms salts widely used as food preservatives — what is it called?
This crested songbird in the crow family sports a black, U-shaped collar and is known for hiding acorns to eat later — which eastern North American bird?
Blue jay: Species of bird. The blue jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to eastern North America.

Unique among mammals, human females are the only ones to permanently develop this secondary sex organ at puberty rather than just during pregnancy, and it later produces milk via the mammary gland — which body part?
Breast: Part of the female primate torso that has mammary glands.
The fifth most abundant element in Earth's crust and a reactive alkaline earth metal, this element's name comes from the Latin word for 'lime' obtained by heating limestone — what is it?
Calcium: Chemical element with atomic number 20 (Ca)
This compound ferries long-chain fatty acids into a cell's mitochondria to be burned for energy and is naturally concentrated in muscles like the heart — what is it?
Carnitine: Compound active in mitochondria. Carnitine is a quaternary ammonium compound involved in metabolism in most mammals, plants, and some bacteria.
In calculus, this formula computes the derivative of a composite function by multiplying together the derivatives of its two component functions — what is it called?

Native to Sri Lanka, the inner bark of this evergreen tree is the original source of a beloved baking spice, sometimes distinguished from a cheaper cousin as the 'true' or 'Ceylon' variety — which tree?
Cinnamomum verum: Species of tree. The inner bark of the tree is historically regarded as the spice cinnamon, though this term was later generalized to include C. cassia as well.
Named for an Indonesian island where an 18th-century naturalist first catalogued it, this pungent, oregano-scented succulent also goes by Cuban oregano and Indian borage — which plant?
Coleus amboinicus: Species of plant. Coleus amboinicus is a species of semi-succulent perennial plant in the family Lamiaceae.
Produced mainly by the adrenal cortex and surging in response to stress and low blood sugar, this steroid hormone is sold as medicine under the name hydrocortisone — what is it?
Built from microfilaments, intermediate filaments, and microtubules, this network gives a cell its shape and lets it contract and migrate — what is it?
Cytoskeleton: Network of filamentous proteins that forms the internal framework of cells.
Carnations and sweet williams both belong to which flowering plant genus of about 340 species, native mainly to Europe and Asia?
Attracted to rotting fruit and fermenting drinks, this insect became the first animal launched into space in 1946 and has earned six Nobel Prizes for scientists who studied it — what is it?
Drosophila melanogaster: Species of fruit fly.
The first woman to win the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, this political scientist earned it in 2009 for her analysis of economic governance, especially the commons — who was she?
This term covers a range of spiritual traditions built around hidden or occult knowledge, appearing in Christian, Buddhist, Hindu, and Quranic contexts alike — what is it?
Esotericism: Topics referred to by the same term.
What is this — “Public exposure of intimate body parts”?

Exhibitionism: Public exposure of intimate body parts. Exhibitionism is the practice of exposing one's intimate parts – such as the breasts, genitals, or buttocks – in a public or semi-public environment.

Sometimes nicknamed a 'cat' though it's actually the sole living member of its own genus in the weasel family, this North American forest mammal has been trapped for its fur since the 1700s — what is it?
Fisher (animal): Species of small, carnivorous mammal native to North America.

In math, this concept assigns exactly one element of a codomain to each element of a domain, and was formalized via set theory by the end of the 19th century after originating as a way to describe how one varying quantity depends on another — what is it called?
Function (mathematics): Association of one output to each input.
Recognized as the world's longest ray-finned fish, this ribbon-shaped, silvery-blue deep-sea creature is often blamed for sea-serpent legends — which fish?
Giant oarfish: Species of oceanic ray-finned fish.
Descended from medieval hunting dogs once used to take down bears, boar, and deer for German nobility, this breed ties with the Irish Wolfhound as one of the world's two largest — which breed is it?
Great Dane: German breed of dog. The Great Dane is a German breed of large mastiff-sighthound, which descends from hunting dogs of the Middle Ages used to hunt bears, wild boar, and deer.
This German-American physicist won a 1967 Nobel Prize for explaining how a nuclear cycle powers heavy stars, after heading the Theoretical Division at Los Alamos during World War II — who is he?
In this condition, part of the stomach slips upward through the diaphragm into the chest, often triggering acid reflux, heartburn, or trouble swallowing — what is it?
Hiatal hernia: Entrance of abdominal organs into the middle chest through the diaphragm.
Also called prussic acid, this toxic, flammable liquid with the formula HCN boils just above room temperature and serves as an industrial precursor to plastics and mining chemicals — what is it?

Also known as the spectacled or binocellate snake, this reptile from South Asia is one of the 'Big Four' species responsible for most snakebites in the region and is revered in Hindu mythology — which snake?
Indian cobra: Species of snake. The species is native to the Indian subcontinent, and is a member of the "Big Four" species that are responsible for the most snakebite cases in Sri Lanka and India.
This English inventor and industrial designer created the bagless vacuum cleaner using cyclonic separation, and by 2023 was the UK's fifth-richest person — who is he?
James Dyson: British inventor and businessman (born 1947)
Back in 1859, this Irish physicist proved the link between atmospheric CO2 and what we now call the greenhouse effect — who was he?
Deafened by childhood illness and rerouted from competitive diving, she became a Hollywood stunt pioneer and earned the title 'the fastest woman in the world.' Who was she?
Kitty O'Neil: American stuntwoman and racer (1946–2018)
Spread through the bite of sandflies, this parasitic disease can appear in cutaneous, mucocutaneous, or visceral forms, the last marked by fever and an enlarged spleen — what is it called?
Leishmaniasis: Disease caused by parasites of the Leishmania type.

This catch-all name covers over 7,000 squamate species on every continent but Antarctica — from finger-length geckos to the three-meter Komodo dragon, with a few 'legless' lineages thrown in. What is it?
Found from Gibraltar to across Asia, these Old World monkeys live in troops centered on dominant matriarchs, and one Malaysian species eats about 70 rats a year — what are they?
Macaque: Genus of Old World monkeys. The macaques constitute a genus (Macaca) of gregarious Old World monkeys of the subfamily Cercopithecinae.
Prized by fur trappers for its yellowish-to-dark-brown coat, this bushy-tailed, weasel-like mammal is adapted to life in the taiga's coniferous forests — what is it?
Nicknamed 'Swallow' as a fighter and 'Storm Bird' as a bomber, this German aircraft was the world's first operational jet-powered fighter, first flying on jet power in 1942 — what was it?
Messerschmitt Me 262: First operational jet-powered fighter aircraft. The design of what would become the Me 262 started in April 1939, before World War II.

This Serbian polymath — mathematician, astronomer, civil engineer — explained Earth's long-term climate swings by tracking our planet's shifting position relative to the Sun, a theory of cycles that now bears his name. Who was he?
Milutin Milanković: Serbian scientist and professor (1879–1958)
Serving King Roger II in Norman Sicily, this Arab geographer created the Tabula Rogeriana, one of the most advanced world maps of the medieval era — who was he?
Known in Sanskrit as Padma or Kamala, this aquatic plant is often called sacred lotus though true water lilies actually belong to a different family — what species?
Nelumbo nucifera: Species of aquatic flowering plant. It is sometimes colloquially called a water lily, though this more often refers to members of the family Nymphaeaceae.
Named for the daring Doolittle airmen of World War II, this subsonic stealth flying wing is being built to replace the B-1 and B-2 by 2040 — which aircraft is it?
Northrop Grumman B-21 Raider: American stealth bomber aircraft.

This dental specialty treats misaligned teeth and jaws, a condition worldwide diets of softer foods have made even more common by leaving smaller jaws with less room to fit them. What specialty is it?
Sold under the brand name Paxil, this SSRI antidepressant treats conditions from panic disorder to PTSD, and is also prescribed for premature ejaculation and menopausal hot flashes — what is it?
Paroxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It has also been used in the treatment of premature ejaculation, and hot flashes due to menopause.
Featuring an R−O−O−R backbone where two oxygen atoms bond directly to each other, what name covers this class of molecules?
Peroxide: Chemical compounds with the structure R–O–O–R'
Manufactured in Switzerland since 1991, this pressurized single-engine turboprop's large aft cargo door has made it popular with air-ambulance operators and police departments alike — which aircraft?
Pilatus PC-12: Swiss executive and utility transport aircraft.
Emerging in the 1960s as scholars from once-colonized nations began writing back, this academic field examines the lingering cultural and political effects of empire — what's it called?
Postcolonialism: Study of the cultural legacy of colonialism and imperialism.
Which medical specialty focuses on diagnosing, treating, and preventing conditions related to cognition, mood, emotion, and behavior, using tools like the DSM-5?
Psychiatry: Branch of medicine devoted to mental disorders.
Native to Southeast Asia and a close relative of the lychee and longan, this medium-sized tree lends its name to a hairy-skinned tropical fruit — what is it?
Rambutan: Southeast Asian fruit. Rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum) is a medium-sized tropical tree in the family Sapindaceae.
Extracted from the seeds of the castor oil plant, this lectin toxin carries an estimated lethal oral dose in humans of about one milligram per kilogram — what is it?
Also called false saffron, this thistle-like annual is one of the world's oldest crops, prized today for the vegetable oil pressed from its seeds — what plant is it?
Safflower: Species of plant. Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius), also false saffron, is a highly branched, herbaceous, thistle-like annual plant in the family Asteraceae.
This synthetic element, number 106, holds the rare distinction of being named after a scientist who was still alive at the time — its most stable isotopes survive mere minutes. What is it?
Seaborgium: Chemical element with atomic number 106 (Sg)

This primate group includes every animal traditionally called a monkey or ape — including humans — and split from the tarsiers roughly 60 million years ago. What's the term for this broader classification?
Also called dinkel wheat, this high-protein relict crop has been a staple in parts of Europe since the Bronze Age and is considered a hexaploid hybrid of common wheat and emmer — what is it?
Spelt: Species of wheat. It is a relict crop, eaten in Central Europe and northern Spain.

This speech disorder involves involuntary repetitions and prolongations of sounds or words, affects roughly 1% of the world's population, and is unrelated to a person's ability to structure their thoughts — what's it called?
Stuttering: Speech disorder. Persistent stuttering into adulthood often leads to outcomes detrimental to overall mental health, such as social isolation and suicidal thoughts.
This genus contains every living species of a large, snout-nosed herbivorous mammal, including the Malayan form sometimes split into its own genus — what is it?
Tapirus: Genus of tapir. The Malayan tapir is usually included in Tapirus as well, although some authorities have moved it into its own genus, Acrocodia.
As head of Harland and Wolff's drafting department, this shipbuilder helped design the Olympic-class liners and went down with the most famous of them on her maiden voyage — who was he?
Thomas Andrews: British businessman and shipbuilder (1873–1912)
Sold as Tramal, this opioid painkiller doubles as an SNRI — which means it carries a rare risk of serotonin syndrome. What is it?
